messages:
Zach (Acme): hey team — we've been getting intermittent failures from the embeddings endpoint. some requests return 768-d vectors, others 1024-d, and our indexing pipeline chokes. started around 2026-02-12 14:07 UTC. we use a cache prefix 'acme-v1' so thought cache reuse might be weird. sample curl below.

Josh S.: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact curl + response headers (x-request-id, x-cache-hit) and a minimal repro? also which model name you're calling in the request?

Zach (Acme): sure — here's a reduced repro (redacted api key):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-1024","input":["hello world","second text"],"cache_prefix":"acme-v1"}'
```

response headers from two runs: 
- run A: x-request-id: r-20260212-001, x-cache-hit: false, x-embed-dims: 1024
- run B (later): x-request-id: r-20260212-027, x-cache-hit: true, x-embed-dims: 768

Josh S.: thanks — that header mismatch is telling. curious if batching was on or if any model fallback happened server-side. tagging eng-ml.

Eva M.: ping — can you confirm whether you have batching enabled client-side or server-side? also what exact model string is in the request payload for the failing runs? sometimes we see dims change when requests are routed to a smaller embedding variant (quantized/low-d) and cache keys don't include the variant.

Zach (Acme): we always set "model":"text-embed-1024". no client batching. we do have an autoswitch rule internally that will try a cheaper variant for cost reasons, but we expected the API to respect the model name. logs show occasional fallback to text-embed-768 at the time of the failing runs. attached snippet from our side: `embedding_request{model=text-embed-1024, prefix=acme-v1, request_id=r-20260212-027}` then later `served_by{model=text-embed-768, node=gpu-15}`

Liam R.: quick note from runtime: earlier this week we pushed a perf change that tightened cache key size and temporarily removed the explicit model_id from the cache key to reduce key length in redis. that would cause different model variants to share the same prefix + input_hash keyspace. there's a rollback queued; can you hold tight while we confirm? commit id was 7d1f2a9 (rolled at 2026-02-11).

Julie O.: i'm seeing a billing blip correlated with these request_ids — some requests billed at the higher token rate and others at the lower, and duplicate charges showed up for ~1200 requests for Acme between 14:05–14:20 UTC. can you paste exact request ids + timestamps?

Zach (Acme): provided a small list earlier, but here are three samples: r-20260212-001 @ 2026-02-12T14:07:03Z, r-20260212-027 @ 2026-02-12T14:12:45Z, r-20260212-031 @ 2026-02-12T14:13:03Z. we saw duplicate response bodies with different dims for the same input hash (so downstream dedupe failed).

SRE-Bot: Automated note: rollback applied to cache-key-change on 2026-02-12T14:16:20Z (deploy id: deploy-1785599000, patch: 7d1f2a9 -> revert-7d1f2a9).

Eva M.: workaround while we finish validation: include the model name in your cache_prefix (eg. "acme-v1::text-embed-1024") or set the client to attach a per-model suffix. also you can toggle strict keying by setting `emb.cache.strict_keying=true` in the private deployment or request `X-Strict-Embed-Key:1` header for hosted. example header: `X-Embed-Prefix: acme-v1::text-embed-1024`.

Liam R.: additional root cause detail — when batching merges were enabled at high QPS, we observed race windows where new routing logic could route some items in a batch to a fallback variant; because the flattened cache key removed model_id, those items could be written/read by other variant requests. revert restores model_id in key. long-term we'll add a guard that refuses to mix variants in the same KV prefix.

Josh S.: we've opened a billing investigation and will credit unexpected duplicate charges pending verification. Julie, liaise with Acme on exact credits. also i'll follow up with product about a guardrail changelist.

Zach (Acme): applied the model-suffixed prefix workaround and re-ran the repro — results steady: all runs now return 1024 dims and x-cache-hit behaves consistently. still seeing a couple of cache misses under heavy concurrency where batching combined inputs and a node temporarily served the 768 variant, but much reduced. thanks for the quick response.

Liam R.: to mitigate the remaining edge-case, enable `emb.cache.strict_keying=true` if you can (hosted header described above) and set `batch.max_items=64` to reduce cross-batch mixing. we'll follow up with a patch to ban cross-variant cache hits entirely.

Julie O.: noted for billing; i'll track credits against the three sample request ids and escalate if more come in.

Josh S.: closing loop for now — follow-up action items: 1) eng-runtime to ship guardrail PR to disallow cross-variant cache reuse, 2) billing to validate credits for Acme, 3) support to share workaround for customers. tagging owners. :white_check_mark:

Zach (Acme): appreciate the help, team. i'll re-open if anything else crops up.
